svg.title: How sign-in works at a faithnet Home: the first time, a new app while signed in, and coming back
svg.desc: An app asks the Home to sign a person in. The Home checks the app against its registry and looks for a Home session. Without one the person proves a credential and, the first time, a Home is made for them. Then the Allow sheet, a delegation signed by the person, its check on chain, a record and a single-use code, and the code exchanged for an id_token. A new app for a person already signed in skips the credential and the new account. An app that still holds its delegation goes straight to the token step. A designed path, live in shadow, records its decision and will skip the sheet and the signature for an app allowed before.
svg.text: How sign-in works at a faithnet Home
One front door for every app. The Home proves who you are. A delegation you sign says what the app may do.
WITHOUT A SESSION
COMING BACK TO AN APP
the app presents the delegation it holds, and the Home answers with a fresh id_token: no page and no prompt
THE NEXT DESIGN, LIVE IN SHADOW
this app was allowed before and asks for nothing more:
no sheet, nothing signed, and the stored wires are checked on chain again
A NEW APP, ALREADY SIGNED IN
the Home session is found:
no credential, no new account
TODAY
Every trip to the Home still ends
at the Allow sheet. The Home now
looks up whether you allowed this
app before, and only records the answer.
Social
Email or phone
Passkey
Wallet
what proves it is you
Social, email and phone sign at the Home. A passkey or a wallet signs on your device.
first time in: every step
a new app, already signed in: skips 4 and 5
coming back to an app: step 10 alone, or no trip at all
the next design, in shadow: will skip 6 and 7
only when needed
